_doc: fc-parallel-010 (system): 3 mixed calls (read_env, run_shell_command, list_processes); no order. The prompt names a distinct tool for each piece of information: env-var lookup for PATH, shell for uname, process-list for ps. Decoys are minimal (each tool is the right one for its piece). Tests the model's ability to do 3 unrelated info-gathering calls in one turn with correct arg shapes per tool. SCORER EDGE CASE (N2, PR #31): the expected list_processes call has arguments {} — a zero-arg call. This is the only case in the suite that pins an empty-args expectation. When the adapter (#19) lands, confirm the one-set arg-matching treats a predicted call with no arguments as equal to expected arguments {} (and does not require an explicit empty object in the predicted <tool_call>). _doc BACKFILL (N3, PR #31): cases 006-010 carry a _doc field but 001-005, fc-single-001..020, and system2-001 do not. Harmless (the field is ignored by the schema) but inconsistent — a future cleanup PR should backfill _doc across the earlier cases.
prompt: Give me a quick system snapshot: the value of PATH, the kernel release (use `uname -r`), and a list of running processes. Use the appropriate tool for each piece.

function.name: run_shell_command
function.description: Execute a shell command in a sandboxed non-interactive shell and return its combined stdout+stderr. Read-only commands are recommended; commands that modify the filesystem require explicit confirmation via `confirm: true`.

confirm.description: Must be true for any command that writes outside /tmp or invokes package managers.

function.name: read_env
function.description: Read the value of a single environment variable. If `name` is omitted, returns a JSON object of {name: value} for every env var. Sensitive variables (anything containing 'SECRET', 'TOKEN', 'KEY', or 'PASSWORD' in the name) are redacted to '<redacted>' for safety.

function.name: list_processes
function.description: Return a snapshot of running processes as a JSON array of {pid, user, command}.
